milestones.title: Foundation, governance, source baseline, and conformance bootstrap
milestones.functional_goal: Create a buildable Rust workspace and machine-enforced migration process without moving any Re-CTM production behavior.
scope: Code, commit, acceptance, architecture, and migration standards
Frozen source contract and graph baseline
Bootstrap golden contract and local gate
non_goals: No OAuth, MCP, Native, workflow, or finalizer cutover
milestones.rollback: Delete the new MTM-reboot repository; Re-CTM remains unchanged and authoritative.

milestones.title: Typed contract and pure policy core
milestones.functional_goal: Move stable side-effect-free contracts and policies to typed Rust while preserving exact source behavior.
milestones.rollback: Return pure calls to the Python reference implementation; no state migration is involved.

milestones.title: Native process lifecycle and isolation plane
milestones.functional_goal: Move process ownership, command lifecycle, toolchain policy, Bubblewrap helper, and tunnel child lifecycle without weakening isolation.
scope: Command IDs, polling, paging, TTY, timeout, kill, and shutdown
milestones.rollback: Switch the helper/process adapter back to Python while preserving command-state compatibility; Rust has no database authority.

milestones.title: Persistence, project state, and capability authority
milestones.functional_goal: Move SQLite migrations, transactional state, project records, and capability authority with one production writer and copied-state differential testing.
scope: Run, domain, branch, steering, project, claim, revision, and reference state
Capability issue, validation, registry cross-check, and revocation
non_goals: No schema version change without a separate record
milestones.rollback: Restore Python authority against a verified compatible database backup; cutover is blocked unless rollback is proven on copied data.

milestones.title: OAuth, MCP, HTTP gateway, and public tool dispatch
milestones.functional_goal: Move the public network boundary while retaining exact OAuth, MCP, catalog, origin, and error behavior.
scope: OAuth DCR, PKCE, codes, tokens, fixed and dynamic origins
Exact 18 Native plus 6 Rethlas public catalog and hidden aliases
milestones.rollback: Route traffic back to the Python gateway without changing persistent state or client-visible endpoints.

milestones.title: Workflow, vault, verifier, finalizer, and project semantics
milestones.functional_goal: Move the mathematical state machine and its sole finalization authority using historical trace replay and verifier-isolation tests.
scope: Task envelopes and deterministic transition plans
Full and compact workflows, branches, join, repair, and escalation
Mechanical verdict, final artifact, and project promotion
milestones.rollback: Return workflow requests to Python before deleting any Python authority; database and artifact compatibility must already be proven.

milestones.title: Remaining tools, integrations, operator UI, and packaging
milestones.functional_goal: Complete the operational binary and distribution without changing migrated authority semantics.
scope: File, Git, search, image, diagnostics, research, and LaTeX adapters
CLI, TUI, Quick Tunnel presentation, and shutdown
Install, upgrade, package, and release artifacts
non_goals: No UI authority over security or workflow
milestones.rollback: Use the prior packaged Python distribution while Rust state and protocols remain compatible.

milestones.title: Full cutover, performance evidence, and Python retirement
milestones.functional_goal: Prove the complete Rust runtime on real targets, exercise rollback, record measured gains, and remove Python production dependencies in a separate final step.
scope: Upgrade, rollback, soak, resource, and performance tests
non_goals: No deletion of historical fixtures or receipts
milestones.rollback: Reinstall the last accepted compatible Python release from immutable artifacts and restore the tested database backup.

events.summary: User approved a new MTM-reboot project with six to eight incremental delivery rounds.
Created the new project and began the foundation/governance milestone without moving production authority.
Pinned Rust 1.98.0, passed governance, architecture, formatting, Clippy, Rust tests, golden contract, and local record gates, and retained Python as sole production authority.
Approved typed contract and pure policy work as the only next actionable migration milestone.
Re-ran the completed MTM-001 gate, confirmed a clean committed baseline, and began typed Rust contract/policy implementation with Python retained as the frozen differential reference.
Entered read-only Rust shadow after typed contracts and policies passed Rust tests and the bounded differential harness was available.
Made Rust authoritative for the MTM-reboot pure contract/policy core after 135 exact Python-Rust comparisons, frozen golden hash, side-effect check, and A5 resource non-regression passed.
Completed MTM-002 with Rust authority limited to side-effect-free MTM-reboot contracts/policies; Re-CTM Python remains the production runtime for every stateful and external component.

Approved Native process lifecycle and isolation as the only next milestone; implementation must begin with an MTM-002 recheck and retain Python production authority until target evidence permits cutover.

Re-ran the committed MTM-002 full gate and 135-case differential corpus, confirmed the frozen hash and clean source-reference files, and began the Native process/isolation milestone without moving production authority.

The Rust Native shadow matched the frozen Python implementation for exact toolchain/Bubblewrap construction and semantic command lifecycle scenarios, with zero mismatches and no Git-visible side effects.

Accepted mtm-native as the authoritative Native implementation inside MTM-reboot after hash-bound real Bubblewrap, private-root, SageMath, Magma, TTY, timeout, kill, helper-protocol and Quick Tunnel evidence passed. Re-CTM remains the deployed Python production authority.
Completed MTM-003 with A0-A5 evidence, accepted iteration/receipt records, implementation-bound target validation and no SQLite, OAuth/MCP, workflow or finalizer migration.
Approved persistence, project state and capability authority as the only next milestone; it must begin with a complete MTM-003 recheck and copied-database rollback baseline.

Re-ran the committed MTM-003 full gate, both frozen differential corpora and implementation-bound target evidence, restored the generated validation report, confirmed a clean repository, and began copied-database persistence and capability work without enabling dual production writes.

Entered copied-database shadow after 52 API/token/physical-state operations matched exactly and v0/v1/v2, future-version, failed-migration and rollback-copy cases passed without touching the deployed writer.

Accepted mtm-storage as the authoritative persistence/capability implementation inside MTM-reboot after transactional tests, cross-runtime tokens, registry tamper denial, real read-only production-state backup equality, writer serialization and exact rollback passed. Re-CTM Python remains the deployed production writer.
Completed MTM-004 with A0-A5 evidence, accepted iteration and receipt records, implementation-bound redacted target validation and no OAuth/MCP, workflow, finalizer or deployed database cutover.

Approved OAuth, MCP, HTTP and public tool dispatch as the only next milestone; it must begin with a complete MTM-004 recheck and preserve the exact 24-tool catalog, OAuth security and one-writer state boundary.

receipts.behavior_before: MTM-reboot had no Rust process ownership, helper protocol, hard-isolation implementation, target CAS execution, TTY lifecycle or tunnel child authority.

receipts.risk_review: The new crate has no SQLite, OAuth, MCP, workflow, vault or finalizer access. Debug-build timing is slower than Python in the small lifecycle harness, so no performance optimization claim is made.
